hardware.cpu: AMD EPYC-Milan, 28 virtual cores per node (ETH LeoMed compute-biomed and gpu-biomed nodes)

notes: Two devices measured 2026-11-14 at apxchol main 7dee3a3a: cpu on a whole 28-core EPYC-Milan node and gpu on one RTX 4090 with 28 cores.
Competitors are capped at max(20 x the best complete apxchol setup + solve on the same matrix and device, 30 s) per solve, from this campaign's own apxchol cells.
C++ series: one warmup and three retained repetitions, 28 OpenMP threads pinned to the job's cores.

Toolchain: Compute Canada StdEnv/2023, LLVM 20.1.8 (AVX2 build) with -march=native, CUDA 13.4.3 with the CUDA forward-compatibility driver library. Serial RCHOL and pRCHOL come from a StdEnv/2026 + LLVM 22.1.8 build, because serial RCHOL fails with the StdEnv/2023 toolchain ('invalid factor diagonal', job 10015602).
RCHOL/pRCHOL use the portable Eigen PCG (no MKL).
ParAC and CMG were not run on LeoMed.

adapt_s is the part of setup_s that the benchmark spent adapting the input for a solver that does not accept a singular or disconnected operator as given. apxchol, AC/AC2, RCHOL and pRCHOL take components natively and report 0.
cap_rule: max(20 x the fastest complete apxchol setup + solve on the same matrix and device, 30 s); a competitor over the cap, or killed at it, is exceeded_cap

columns.rel_res: largest ||b-Ax||/||b|| over the retained repeats, on the original system
columns.setup_s: seconds, from the repeat with the median setup + solve
columns.adapt_s: seconds of setup_s that the benchmark spent adapting the input for this solver (component discovery, Dirichlet pins, component slicing); 0 when the solver takes the input natively, empty when the campaign did not measure it
columns.cap_s: the competitor's time cap, when one applied
columns.class: grids, meshes (meshes and circuits), ipm (linear programs), social (social and web graphs)
